item.title: Why Draymond Green suggested he come off the Warriors' bench, and why Steve Kerr said no
item.description: The Warriors' Draymond Green, center, yells after scoring between Trail Blazers forward Deni Avdija, left, and center Donovan Clingan on Friday. (Craig Mitchelldyer/Associated Press) PORTLAND, Ore. - This, last week, came one of the few times that coach Steve Kerr would ever shut Draymond Green 's foresight down. They talked on the road, as they do, because things were going wrong. Losing. Losing because of bad process. And so the 36-year-old Green tried to jump ahead, to anticipate, the greatest skill in what Kerr firmly believes is a first-ballot Hall of Fame career. Green told Kerr he'd come off the Golden State Warriors bench, if needed. Just like that. No hemming and hawing. For a man whose entire basketball existence and greatness and controversy has been carved from his own razor-sharp pride, this was a rather remarkable admission of mortality. Why? Why volunteer this? "Because," Green told the Chronicle Friday night, after the Warriors' 116-94 loss to Portland. He pondered. Five seconds passed, as he computed. He settled on the simplest of explanations. "S- wasn't working," Green continued. "So, something's not working, you gotta change something. As a guy who's been here for 15 years and has done what I've done - it's not easy for a coach to be like, ‘All right, I'm gonna do that.' So my mindset is, ‘If that's the case, and it's not easy for you, how about I make it easy for you?'" Kerr, of course, said no. He needed Green to set the tone defensively, in Stephen Curry 's continued absence. Kerr was vindicated in two subsequent wins, as Green locked up Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum last Sunday and dished out 11 assists against the Sacramento Kings on Wednesday. Green was challenged, again, on Friday, as the Trail Blazers hardly bothered to guard Green in yet another factor that clogged up Golden State's offense in a brutal start. This will only continue to be a wider topic of discussion beyond Golden State's walls - prudent enough that it blossomed inside Green's own supercomputer of a brain - as long as the Warriors struggle offensively in any Curry absence. Green is still excellent defensively and a core facilitator, but is averaging just 3.7 points per game (his lowest figure since his rookie year) on 38.3% shooting from the field. That is certainly acceptable when Curry's gravity helps Green create for the other three on the floor, but often becomes a vortex when Curry's off of it. The Warriors' net rating in lineups with Green and without Curry is -23.4 this season, according to Databallr; albeit a smaller sample size, that would easily stand as the worst mark in any season of the pair's 15-year partnership. If Kerr relents, and turns to Green off the bench before Curry's (now-creeping) return, it'll be met with acceptance. item.title: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani turns to Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum for Achilles hope
item.description: The NBA has been beset by a rash of Achilles tendon injuries, perhaps none more high-profile than star Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum's, sustained in the 2025 NBA Eastern Conference Semifinals second round series vs. the New York Knicks . And the St. Louis native has been putting in work behind the scenes using his own experience to help his peers in the league navigate such a consequential injury, his own recovery serving as a model for them to follow. So with all that in mind, that the Mayor of New York City, popular rising populist star Zohran Mamdani invoked the Celtics star when working his way back to health after his own Achilles tear, suffered in a recent pickup soccer game Mamdani was evidently not properly prepared for the rigors of. Ahead of his Achilles tendon surgery on Friday (Nov. 27), Mamdani reassured himself as much as the assembled media with regard to the procedure while looking to the Celtics star as an example of what could be for his damaged appendage. "I keep telling myself, Jayson Tatum did it, anything is possible," said the New York mayor, perhaps sneaking a paraphrased Kevin Garnett quote for good measure. "I'm scared, it's my first surgery," he admitted. ""I'll be down from 9 a.m. to about 2 p.m. ... "'m going to be laid out for probably a couple days.." With a return to action that brief, it might be Mamdani future NBA players turn to when in need of Achilles tendon injury guidance. item.title: Russell beats champion Antonelli to Qatar pole
item.description: George Russell took his first pole since the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in September [Getty Images] George Russell led Kimi Antonelli to a one-two as Mercedes dominated qualifying at the Qatar Grand Prix. Russell set two laps quick enough for pole and headed the new world champion by 0.128 seconds. Lando Norris in the McLaren was third, but 0.480secs off the pace, and 0.07secs ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri. And on the two-by-two grid among the top six, there was a surprise at Red Bull as Isack Hadjar edged four-time champion Max Verstappen for fifth by 0.041secs. Ferrari were a lowly seventh and ninth, Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton, who was also beaten by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad. It was Mercedes' first one-two in qualifying since the Canadian Grand Prix in June. But despite their achievement, there was some tension at Mercedes as Antonelli complained about being sent out at the head of the queue on the final laps. "We need to review with the team," Antonelli said, after paying tribute to Russell for doing a "great job", "because that last run I wanted to go at the back but they sent me first." Russell, though, was serene and unconcerned, at least after qualifying. "The car has been brilliant this weekend, a joy to drive but all sessions I was behind Kimi," the Briton said. "But come qualifying I had a really good feeling." Explaining why Mercedes were so far ahead this weekend, Russell said: "Since we brought the upgrade in Malaysia this is the first real high-speed circuit. We've just been refining the set-up and we have always been quick here." McLaren had not looked like being the next best team but Norris ended up beating the fastest Red Bull by 0.116secs - albeit that the fastest Red Bull was not driven by the usual driver. "Certainly the best position we could get out of it today," Norris said. "The fact we were P3 and P4 as a team is all we can ask for. A good day for us. "P3 would be a win for us tomorrow. The Mercedes have been 0.4, 0.5, 0.6secs faster every lap this weekend. We will try and get past them and get in the middle of them but we're kind of not in their race." Ferrari's lack of pace was the most startling, though - Leclerc was a massive 1.260secs off pole. But at least the Ferrari drivers are not starting alongside each other for the first race since they collided in Las Vegas last weekend. Leclerc said he believed the problem stemmed from the smooth asphalt at Losail. "We are very, very far from the guys in front," he said. "I will take that as an opportunity for the team to try and understand because clearly there is something not working with this type of track. "People might wonder because it's not a very specific track layout but it is a definitely a very specific Tarmac, being very smooth and there are quite a few things that tell us the problem might come from that. "There is no quick fix to that but it is hopefully something we can learn from and hopefully have a solution going in the future." Top 10 1. G

item.title: Brentford aim for 'special things' after ending 89-year Old Trafford wait
item.description: Keith Andrews had never been a first-team manager prior to his appointment at Brentford [Getty Images] "Slightly surreal." That is how Brentford manager Keith Andrews summed up the club's first win at Manchester United in 89 years. And the Bees ended their near nine-decade wait for a victory at Old Trafford in some style - thrashing Mauricio Pochettino's strugglers 4-0 on Saturday. Brentford's last win at United before this weekend was in February 1937 - the longest any side has gone between victories against the Red Devils, surpassing Bristol City's 69-year wait between 1909 and 1978. Granted, Brentford had only played eight games on United's turf since then, given the clubs' contrasting fortunes. But the emphatic way in which they ended that streak is surely cause for celebration for a club who just 12 years ago were competing in League One. "Slightly surreal if I am honest," Andrews told BBC Match of the Day. "We have been keen to enjoy the journey. We want to be really ambitious but [with a] level of humility. I think we can achieve special things because I think it is a special group." Brentford have cemented their status as an established Premier League club but "special things" suggests Andrews sees his side going even further. After a second consecutive 4-0 win, having thumped Everton by the same score on Monday, the Bees are fifth in the league and with European football in their sights. Andrews surpassing expectation Andrews' appointment at Brentford in 2025 divided opinion after the departure of Thomas Frank, who had rightly earned the adoration of the fans having led them to the top flight. While some fans trusted the judgement of the board, others suggested hiring someone who had never been a first-team manager before showed a lack of ambition. There can now be little debate around Andrews' position. The Irishman was handed a new contract in February - just eight months into the job - and after finishing 10th last season, he has his sights set on more this campaign. "I haven't been doing this for very long, but it has been a special week," the 46-year-old told Sky Sports after the win at Old Trafford. "I thought we were well worthy of getting the three points. We could have been more clinical and that was the message at half-time. "Could we take the handbrake off more? Could we go for it? I fancy us all the time when we're in those areas. "Twelve games in and we're in a good groove. We feel we do a lot of things right." The former midfielder's strategy to go for more rather than defend their 2-0 half-time lead speaks volumes for how he views the potential in his side - and it ultimately paid off as they further punished United's frailties. item.description: Elche CF v Atletico de Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Atletico Madrid made it three wins in a row with a nervy 3-2 victory at the Estadio Manuel Martinez Valero, where a blistering first-half display was followed by an uncomfortable evening protecting their lead against relegation-threatened Elche. The result keeps Diego Simeone's side third in La Liga on 31 points. Simeone's men could hardly have started faster. Alejandro Grimaldo won a penalty when Federico Redondo brought him down and converted it in the fifth minute, and Lee Kang-in doubled the lead just two minutes later. Martim Neto pulled one back for the hosts in the 26th minute, but Julian Alvarez restored the two-goal cushion before the break, converting a pass from Alex Baena. The second half was a different story. Buba Sangare's long-range strike three minutes after the restart gave Elche belief, and the hosts had 55 per cent of the ball after the interval as Atletico failed to land a single shot on target. Jonathan David missed the visitors' best chance in the 58th minute, while Jan Oblak had to deny Lucas Cepeda and Grady Diangana before Atletico saw the game out. (Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images) Getty Noah Gragson has a contract for the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series season. What happens beyond that could largely depend on what he does over the next 36 points-paying races. Front Row Motorsports extended Gragson’s contract this past summer, giving the 28-year-old another season behind the wheel of the No. 4 Ford. But with the 2026 campaign officially in the books, the organization’s leadership is making its expectations for next year abundantly clear. During a recent appearance on SiriusXM NASCAR Radio, Front Row Motorsports general manager Jerry Freeze delivered a particularly candid assessment of Gragson’s performance and long-term prospects with the organization. “So we do have some continuity with him, and I think it’s time to put up the numbers, or maybe this isn’t working out,” Freeze said. “And I think he feels that way, and we certainly feel that way.” For Gragson, who has spent much of his Cup Series career bouncing between organizations, the upcoming season represents an opportunity to establish some long-term job security. But he’s going to have to earn it. View this post on Instagram Front Row Motorsports Wants More From Noah Gragson in 2027 Gragson enters his third season with Front Row Motorsports having yet to replicate the success he enjoyed in NASCAR’s lower national series. The good news for Gragson is that Freeze still believes in his ability. The general manager pointed to his previous success with JR Motorsports and Kyle Busch Motorsports, as well as encouraging stretches of his Cup Series career, including his performance in the 2026 season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. The problem has been putting those performances together consistently. “I feel like the last part of the year, it looked like it was going in the right direction to me,” Freeze said. “Even if you just look at where we’re at in the points, it’s our lowest-performing car, however many hundred and some points behind the other cars.” With teammates Todd Gilliland and Zane Smith providing an internal benchmark, Front Row Motorsports has a fairly straightforward way of measuring the No. 4 team’s progress next season. Freeze did, however, acknowledge that Gragson hasn’t exactly enjoyed the most stable introduction to Cup Series racing. His first full-time opportunity with Legacy Motor Club in 2023 ended prematurely. He subsequently joined Stewart-Haas Racing in 2024, only for the organization to cease operations at the conclusion of the season. item.title: Thrilling draw in Stuttgart
item.description: Thrilling draw in Stuttgart Ansgar Knauff and Younes Ebnoutalib got the goals as Eintracht twice came from behind to earn a 2-2 draw at VfB Stuttgart. Two fresh faces Head coach Adi Hütter made two changes to his starting line-up for the trip to Stuttgart, with Elias Baum coming in for Keita Kosugi, and Mario Götze replacing Noel Aseko. Chances for Eintracht The two sides initially cancelled each other out, with plenty of intensity in the challenges. After 16 minutes, Jonathan Burkardt attempted an overhead kick inside the penalty area to provide the first real moment of excitement. Two minutes later, Lilian Brassier fired towards the VfB goal from a corner, but his effort was blocked by Maximilian Mittelstädt. Frankfurt grow into the game The Eagles continued to apply pressure and, just before the half-hour mark, birthday boy Farès Chaibi broke into the penalty area but dragged his shot wide of the left-hand post. Prömel puts Stuttgart ahead Frankfurt’s defence had been solid all game but it was undone in the 42 nd minute by Ermedin Demirovic’s pass to Grischa Prömel, who left Noah Atubolu no chance from 11 metres out. Knauff levels In first-half stoppage time, Ansgar Knauff fired towards the VfB goal following a corner. It took a deflection off Deniz Undav, causing the ball to loop beyond the goalkeeper and send the teams in level at 1-1. Jaquez scores, Ebnoutalib equalises Shortly after the restart, Frankfurt’s defence lost track of Luca Jaquez following a cross from Undav, allowing him to head past Atubolu from close range (53’). However, Eintracht responded perfectly to falling behind again. Following a lovely move involving Knauff and Burkardt, Younes Ebnoutalib fired a low shot into the bottom-right corner from 11 metres to make it 2-2 (62’). The match subsequently developed into an end-to-end thriller with chances for both teams. However, neither side was able to add to the scoreline, leaving each with a deserved point.

item.description: There is a song Leeds United supporters sing during games about passports and Daniel Farke. It is about dreaming of a return to Europe and is usually heard when the German's side are winning. At a rain-soaked Elland Road on Saturday, fans belted it out time and time again as their side turned on the style to dispose of Coventry City 3-0 and climb to sixth in the Premier League, having sealed a third-straight top-flight win for the first time since 2021. Two goals from Sean Longstaff - after Dominic Calvert-Lewin had opened the scoring - secured the points and maintained Leeds' winning momentum after back-to-back victories over Tottenham and Chelsea. The Whites have not competed in Europe since 2002, but Farke has got supporters believing a return to continental action might not be far away. "They deserve to dream, think big," Farke told BBC Sport about fans' European dreams. "They should feel the joy." However, the Leeds boss insisted he would not be allowing his players to get carried away - despite their impressive form. "We are in our second season after promotion, second season is normally tough. We will stay focused and concentrated," Farke added. 'Phenomenal and relentless' Leeds' transformation over the past 12 months has been nothing short of remarkable. However, Farke changed the shape of the team at half-time - switching to a three-man central defence - and an improved second-half performance in Manchester bought the under-pressure manager some time. Since then Leeds have gone from strength to strength - and return to Etihad Stadium on Wednesday having picked up 56 points from the past 37 games. Since Farke switched to that three-man central defence, Leeds have reached an FA Cup semi-final, won 13 Premier League games, drawn 17 and lost just seven. item.title: ‘I’ve made huge strides forward’ - Ansgar Knauff reflects on Stuttgart draw
item.description: ‘I’ve made huge strides forward’ - Ansgar Knauff reflects on Stuttgart draw Eintracht Frankfurt twice came from behind to secure a 2-2 draw against Stuttgart on Saturday, with goals from Ansgar Knauff and Younes Ebnoutailib cancelling out efforts from Grischa Prömel and Luca Jaquez. Speaking to Sky after the clash, Man of the Match Knauff was pleased with his individual contribution and the team's overall display, but admitted that the result left him with mixed feelings. “I think I’ve made huge strides forward in the last few weeks,” Knauff told Sky. “I already played well last week against Hoffenheim, and I think I was able to confirm that again today with a solid performance. “And yeah, I’m glad that I think I’ve found my place in the team a little bit now. “I think we played a very good game overall, creating good counterattacking opportunities ,” he explained. The winger also discussed Frankfurt's tactical approach, revealing that the team had deliberately planned to start at full intensity and put Stuttgart under pressure from the opening minutes. “Yeah, definitely. I think that was our plan. We already knew they had played three days ago. We wanted to go full throttle right from the start, put them under pressure. “It worked well for us time and again, especially in the first half." However, while he was pleased with Frankfurt's overall performance, Knauff could not hide his disappointment at the final result. "I'm frustrated in the end that we didn't win ,” he admitted. “But I think we can be very satisfied with today's performance overall.” “Towards the end, I think it was an open game where it could have gone either way,” Knauff concluded.

item.title: Warriors Trade Path to $112 Million ‘Sharpshooter’ Laid Out
item.description: Trey Murphy III #25 of the New Orleans Pelicans Getty Things will change for the Golden State Warriors after December 15. That’s not because Stephen Curry might be back by then (fingers are crossed by the Bay that his return will be sooner), but because the team could find itself ready to make the much-anticipated trade of Kristaps Porzingis then. The Warriors can trade Porzingis now, but because other teams have players who can’t be dealt until the middle of next month, and because teams are still weighing their own futures, the post-December 15 date is the one the organization has its eye on. Unofficially, around the NBA, that is considered the first day of trade season. And Porzingis is one of the most fascinating cases, because he is not going to play this season but his $20 million contract (with only $3 million guaranteed for next year) can be traded as a means for teams seeking to cut payroll, avoid aprons and/or move off an unwanted contract. It’s unlikely that Porzingis will be traded exactly on December 16, but it’s also unlikely the Warriors will wait until the February deadline to move him. Warriors Will Have Options At the San Francisco Chronicle, beat writer Luca Evans had four targets for the Warriors, including Naz Reid, Myles Turner and Daniel Gafford, all big guys who could be useful in replacing Porzingis, but who come with their own flaws. But there has been buzz around the league that the Warriors won’t necessarily go for a center in a move for Porzingis–they could simply go for the best player they can get. And that would likely be Trey Murphy. Evans lays out the package for Murphy–who has been frequently connected to the Dubs–that the Warriors could offer: “Package Porzingis, Moody and draft capital for Murphy, who would have league-wide interest if he’s truly on the trade block and would likely command a significantly higher asking price.” what a night for Trey Murphy III 🤩25 PTS6 STL2 REB pic.twitter.com/g0Bc26m1DO — New Orleans Pelicans (@PelicansNBA) November 28, 2026 Trey Murphy Struggling With Knee Issues That would be an attractive package from the Warriors, who would welcome Murphy’s production, as well as his reasonable contract. Murphy is in the second of a four-year, $112 million deal. Evans notes Murphy is, “a 6-foot-8 sharpshooter who averaged 21.5 points per game last season. While dealing with knee troubles this season, though, Murphy has dropped to 15.1 points per game on a lost Pelicans team.” And he quoted a personnel executive: “Trey is a whole other level of swing, good pairing with Yaxel (Lendeborg) for the future of the team as well, would cost multiple firsts. … If I’m G.S., I would part with picks for Trey.” The countdown is on for the Warriors. item.description: PLAYER RATINGS | VfB Stuttgart 2-2 Eintracht Frankfurt – Thrilling Bundesliga ‘Top-Spiel’ ends all square The 2026/27 Bundesliga’s Saturday evening matchday 11 “Top-Spiel” has ended without a winner. Sebastian Hoeneß’ VfB Stuttgart and Adi Hütter’s Eintracht Frankfurt split the difference in a floodlight encounter at the MHP Arena. An eminently entertaining match between the Swabian hosts and their Hessen guests ultimately proved worthy of its billing. A lively start fails to produce goals Neither team shied away from risks in the opening minutes. Deniz Undav – keen to put his early season form woes behind him – pressed forward alongside attacking partners Grischa Prömel and Ermedin Demirovic. The trio occupying the top two VfB attacking axes nevertheless accomplished little beyond getting in each other’s way. At the other end of the pitch, Eintracht too tended to trip over their own feet heading forward. Jonathan Burkardt (16th minute) and Lilian Brassier (18th minute) were finally able to get a pair of quality chances off once the level of play caught up with the energy in the SGE legs. Frankfurt survive red card scare After finally building up some momentum, the Hessian guests looked to be shackled by a Robin Koch red card in the 20th minute. The Eintracht captain appeared to cut down Demirovic when the Stuttgart striker had a clear path to the net. Match official Sascha Stegemann, compelled to take another look at the scene by the VAR team, observed that Koch’s sliding challenge was actually fair. Stegemann withdrew the red shown to Koch and the match continued at a frenetic pace. Clear chances at goal were nonetheless still lacking. An entertaining first half finally gets some goals The two sides threw themselves wholeheartedly into the direct duels and observers were treated to plenty of pacy passing and crunching tackles. Burkardt tested Dennis Seimen with an effort in the 29th minute. One minute later, Noah Atubolu gathered an effort from Maximilian Mittelstädt. Jeff Chabot did well to defuse a Farès Chaïbi shot in the 34th. Just when it appeared as if neither team would be rewarded for their steady efforts, the deserved breakthrough finally came. Hoeneß’ decision to deploy Prömel as an attacker paid off in the 42nd minute. A lightning-quick attacking charge involving Jamie Leweling and Demirovic unleashed Prömel on the right. item.title: 90% of Browns fans think Cleveland is beating Las Vegas tomorrow
item.description: It’s time for another week of Browns reacts results! The Browns were on the bye this past week, were promoted to Sunday Night Football, and saw all three of their AFC North foes lose (although the Steelers also won this past Friday after a chaotic few days in the headlines). Week-to-week, fan confidence decreased by 6 percentage points down to 82%. I wouldn’t read too much into the decline from 88%; overall, it basically maintained the optimistic perspective. By comparison, 92% of Raiders fans are confident in the direction of their team. That’s a really high amount that I can only assume is elevated by the team having a decent start, coupled with the excitement of getting to see their first overall pick in action now. Browns fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Browns polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Dawgs By Nature fans. Then discuss the results with the Dawg Pound. Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Besides the confidence meter, the main question we asked this week was what fans think the outcome of this Sunday’s Raiders vs. Browns game will be. An astounding 90% of fans think the Browns will win the game, which might be the most lopsided margin I’ve seen since running these types of polls. Fans might be feeling good like I was about Cleveland’s chances, but we just have to hope that weather doesn’t tip the X-Factor toward Las Vegas’ favor . Breaking that percentage down further, 64% of overall fans think the Browns will win a close game, while 26% think Cleveland will win big. The remaining 10% of fans voted for a Raiders victory. Here’s what one optimistic Browns fan said in regards to his vote: I believe they get an early lead and then pressure the heck out of Mendoza the rest of the game. The Browns made great strides last game with ZERO pre-snap penalties. They need to sustain that while also getting a fast start , especially on offense. The Raiders give up a lot of points, so they’re ripe for getting beat badly IF (not the capitals) the Browns can get off to a fast start. Another fan praised the Raiders for starting their rookie quarterback, but still sees a Cleveland victory: I think the Raiders are moving ahead while putting the rookie in. It was a good move for them. I think it will be another tight Browns win 27-24. According to FanDuel , the Browns are 4.5 point favorites against the Raiders this week, with the over/under being 39.5.
